meta.title: Los verbos modales de probabilidad
meta.subtitle: must, might, could y can't para el presente y el pasado, y should have

blocks.title: Después de este pdf sabrás
bullets: indicar lo seguro que estás con must, might, may, could y can't
hacer lo mismo sobre el pasado con must have, might have, can't have
expresar arrepentimiento y crítica con should have
decir lo que fue posible con could have

head: Verbo
Seguridad
Ejemplo
Español
rows: She must be tired. She worked all night.
That can't be Tom. He's in Spain.

blocks.title: must = deber de
blocks.text: Con este sentido must no es una obligación sino una conclusión, como deber de: Debe de ser rico = He must be rich. Lo contrario es can't, no mustn't: No puede ser verdad = That can't be true. Y puede que lleva subjuntivo en español, pero en inglés might va con el verbo sin nada: puede que llueva = it might rain.
Para una conclusión sobre el pasado se usa verbo modal + have + participio.

head: Forma
Ejemplo
Español
rows: The ground is wet. It must have rained.
She might have missed the bus.
Puede que haya perdido el autobús.
Puede que haya tenido un retraso.
You can't have seen him. He was abroad.

blocks.title: have, no of
blocks.text: Al hablar, must have suena como 'must've', y mucha gente escribe por error must of. Es incorrecto. Escribe siempre must have, should have, could have.

head: Forma
Ejemplo
Español
rows: No hacía falta que compraras flores.

blocks.title: debería haber = should have
blocks.text: Debería haberlo sabido o Tendría que haberlo sabido = I should have known. El inglés no cambia should: el pasado está en have + participio. Nunca I should knew ni I must have to know.

rows: He mustn't be at home. The lights are off.
He can't be at home. The lights are off.
Después de must no va to.
It must have rained last night.

blocks.text: Completa con el verbo modal o la forma correcta. Las respuestas están en la última página.

items.q: You've been travelling all day. You ______ be exhausted.
items.full: You've been travelling all day. You must be exhausted.

items.q: That ______ be Anna. She's in Australia.
items.full: That can't be Anna. She's in Australia.

items.q: Take an umbrella. It ______ rain later.
items.full: Take an umbrella. It might rain later.

items.q: The window is broken. Somebody must ______ thrown a stone.
items.full: The window is broken. Somebody must have thrown a stone.

items.q: I ______ have studied more. I failed the test.
items.full: I should have studied more. I failed the test.

items.q: She can't have ______ the letter. It's still here.
items.full: She can't have sent the letter. It's still here.

items.q: We ______ have won if we had played better.
items.full: We could have won if we had played better.

items.q: You ______ have told me! I didn't know.
items.full: You should have told me! I didn't know.

items.q: He isn't answering. He ______ be asleep.
items.full: He isn't answering. He may be asleep.

items.q: They're late. They might have ______ the train.
items.full: They're late. They might have missed the train.
